MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L11·N7823unmasked layer
Fires on sentence-boundary punctuation — mostly a period (or colon) closing a descriptive clause in scraped/SEO-style web text (hotel/facility blurbs, machinery spam), and occasionally on a word-piece just before such a break; the same ".\n" token can strongly suppress it in other contexts, so it's a punctuation/clause-boundary detector rather than a semantic one.

L11·N11135unmasked layer
This neuron fires on ordinary function/connective words mid-clause in continuous prose (e.g. "of" in "period of time", "in order", "according to", "the use of"), while being strongly suppressed at "?" or "!" immediately followed by a newline (headline/call-to-action boundaries) — i.e. it tracks "sentence still flowing" vs. "punctuated line break."

L11·N12921unmasked layer
This neuron tracks positions inside comma-separated enumerations — it peaks on the last/penultimate list item or the comma just before the closing "and …" (e.g. "Methodists, Atheists…", "Calzones, Sandwiches, Salads", "Costa Rica, Thailand and India"), with the same list-delimiter commas driving the strongest negative values, so it is a structural list-boundary detector rather than a semantic one.
